INTELLIGENT COMBATANTS CONTINUED
TARGETING PRIORITY
An Intelligent Combatants AI Steps will usually specify which figure will be targeted when an Intelligent Combatant takes an Action or uses Abilities. Sometimes, this will be something specific like the opponent with the lowest HP, or the target with the lowest Armor Value. Other times, it simply doesn’t specify.
In both cases, players will refer to the specific Action being used to determine eligible targets. For Attack Actions, targets must be within the listed Range and within Line of Sight. For Spell Actions, targets must be within SOI. If the AI Step of an Intelligent Combatant further specifies a target, targets meeting the specific criteria are considered the eligible targets for that Action.
If a specific target is never mentioned, or if there are ever multiple eligible targets even after a more specific target is identified, Combatants will prioritize the target that is closer to the front of the Initiative Track.
Example: An AI Step instructs a Cave Sickle to make a ATK against the target with the most Damage. There are 2 eligible targets, both are within Range, which is adjacent, and they both have the same amount of Damage. Out of the two, the target closer to the front of the Initiative Track would be the target of the Attack.
“UP TO” VS “WITHIN”
If an Intelligent Combatant Card references “up to” in its AI Steps, then the Combatant will attempt to use the maximum value if able. If they cannot, then they will use as much as they can.
If an Intelligent Combatant Card references “within,” then the Combatant will use the Action or Ability without consideration to maximum Ranges or values.
Example: The Animate’s Intelligent Combatant Card says “Move up to 2 spaces farther from the target.”
This means the Animate will always move 2 spaces farther from their target unless they cannot. In that case, they will move as many spaces as they are able.
If the Animate’s Intelligent Combatant Card instead said, “Move to be within 4 spaces of the nearest opponent.” then the Animate would find the nearest opponent. If that opponent was already 4 or fewer spaces away, then the Animate would not move at all. Otherwise, it would move until it was within 4 spaces of the nearest opponent.
IMPORTANT: Some Abilities that Adventurers control will use the language “up to” when referring to things like moving and range. In the case of an Adventurer controlling the Ability, they are not required to use the maximum listed spaces.
“NEAREST” AND “FARTHEST”
Intelligent Combatant Cards will sometimes reference Nearest or Farthest. When determining what space, target, or figure is Nearest or Farthest, players should count out the number of spaces in the shortest path to the space, target, or figure using the limitations and rules for the Action in question. (Such as the rules for Movement, Range, or SOI.)
If the Action in question does not have rules to follow for counting range, count out spaces at a 1-for-1 conversion, counting diagonally if necessary, to the target figures or spaces.
Obstructing Terrain spaces can never be counted through when determining this distance.
MOVING “FARTHER”
Intelligent Combatant Cards will sometimes instruct a Combatant to move farther from a space or a figure. When this occurs the Combatant will move one space farther away from the target or space following normal movement rules.
“TOWARDS & AWAY”
If an Intelligent Combatant Card references “Towards” in its AI Steps, then the Combatant will only move into spaces that are closer to the destination listed in its AI. This movement does not necessarily need to be in a straight line. If the destination is a space occupied by another figure, the destination becomes the nearest adjacent space to the figure.
If an Intelligent Combatant Card references “Away” in its AI Steps, then the Combatant will only move into spaces that are farther from the destination listed in its AI. This movement does not necessarily need to be in a straight line.
If an Intelligent Combatant's AI Step says to move “Towards” or “Away” and there is more than one option available, they will always choose the option that is the most beneficial position possible for themselves.
When determining or counting if a space is farther or closer when referencing “Towards” or “Away”, always use the rules for counting movement.
“THEN”
Sometimes, AI Steps have instructions to perform individual Abilities or Actions separated by the word “THEN”. When this occurs, the current Ability or Action being performed ends and a new line of instruction begins.
It’s possible that an AI Step cannot do all of the listed “THEN” steps in its instructions. In these cases, it will skip the current “THEN” in the AI Step.
IMPORTANT: Players must always check if the AI Step has “CONTINUE DOWN” listed, even if the “THEN” instructions above it couldn’t be fulfilled.
Is there an opponent within SOI?
Cast a SPELL 6, prioritizing the opponent with the lowest Conviction Value without Darkness. Inflict Darkness.
THEN: Make a 4 ATK, prioritizing an opponent with Darkness.
THEN: Move towards the nearest opponent.
THEN: Make a ATK against the opponent with the most Damage.
Example: The Animate has an AI Step with the following condition: “Is there an opponent within SOI?”
Assuming this is true, the Animate will cast a Spell that inflicts Darkness.
THEN, it will make a Ranged Attack prioritizing an opponent with Darkness. If no Adventurers were Inflicted with Darkness, the Animate would attack any opponent within Range 4.
THEN, it will move towards the nearest opponent (Attempting to get as close as possible.).
The next THEN instruction explains that the Animate will Attack an adjacent opponent. If there is no adjacent opponent for the Animate to Attack, it will do nothing. Since the Animate doesn’t “CONTINUE DOWN” at the end of this AI Step, its activation would end.
IMPORTANT: Intelligent Combatants will always consider only the possible targets for an Action unless they specifically state otherwise. For example, if an Attack would target the figure with the most Damage, it will target the figure with the most Damage in Range.

INTELLIGENT COMBATANT TURN WALKTHROUGH
EXAMPLE 1
The Animate begins with the Start of Turn Phase. There are no Abilities that occur in the Start of Turn or Status Phases, so the Animate moves on to the Activation Phase. This Animate is adjacent to 3 Adventurers and has 3 Damage tokens on its card. At the start of the Activation Phase, players check the Animate's card to make sure there are no relevant Passive Abilities that may occur during the Animate's turn. Both of the Animate's Passive Abilities happen when the Animate is Attacking, so the players will keep those Abilities in mind as they continue to the Animate's AI Steps.
Since the Animate has Damage tokens on its card (A), its first AI Step's bolded condition (D) is true. This means that the Animate will HEAL 2. The player removes 2 Damage tokens from the Animate, making its total Damage 1.
Since the AI Step has CONTINUE DOWN listed in its instructions, the players continue to the next bolded condition (E).
The second AI Step occurs if there is at least 1 opponent adjacent to the Animate. Since there are 3 opponents adjacent, the Condition is true.
The Animate makes a ATK. Since the AI Step did not specify a target and there are 3 eligible targets, players check to see which Adventurer's Initiative Card is closer to the front of the Initiative Track. In this example, Rook's Initiative Card is at the front of the Initiative Track (I), so he is the target.
The Animate builds its Combat Dice Pool using its listed Combat Dice (H) of WHITE and PURPLE. Checking the Passive Ability Heavy Cleave (C), the players determine that it will occur during this Attack since this is the first Attack the Animate will make against an adjacent opponent this turn. So the Animate adds the BLACK to its Combat Dice Pool.
Rook declines to Dodge and the Animate rolls a WHITE 6 and PURPLE 3 for a total of 9. It also rolls 6 and 2.
This beats Rook's Defense Value by 2 and the Attack hits.
During the Determining Damage Step of the Attack, the Animate spends 2 and 2 to add +2 PHYSICAL DMG (G). Including the difference rolled to hit, the PHYSICAL DMG determined is 4. (A difference of 2, and +2 Physical Damage from symbols.)
The Damage would then be reduced by Rook's Armor Value, but since he has no items equipped with an Armor Value, his Armor Value is 0 so the Damage is not reduced.
The Final Damage of the Attack is 4 and Rook adds 4 Damage tokens to his card.
After the Animate concludes its Attack, it would normally continue to the next "THEN" in the AI Step. However, since it hit with an Attack, the Passive Ability Chains of Perdition (B) is used, and the Animate Attacks the same target again.

core_rules.mechanic_description: The Animate doesn't add the BLACK to its Combat Dice Pool via Heavy Cleave.
Rook has the option to Dodge again but declines.
The Animate rolls a WHITE 7, and a PURPLE 3 for a total of 10.
The Attack beats Rook's Defense Value by 3, resulting in a hit.
The Animate spends 2 and 2 to add +2 PHYSICAL DMG. Then, the Animate spends its 1 to add +2 PHYSICAL DMG. This brings the total added Damage via symbols to +4 PHYSICAL DMG.
The total PHYSICAL DMG determined is 7. (A difference rolled of 3, and +4 Physical Damage from symbols.)
The Damage would be reduced by Rook's Armor Value, but, again, his Armor Value is 0 so the Damage is not reduced. The Final Damage of the Attack is 7 and Rook adds 7 more Damage tokens to his card.
This would bring Rook's total Damage to 11. Since Rook has 14 Health, he's still on the board, ready to fight.

Now that the Attack granted by Chains of Perdition has ended, the Animate continues its AI Step. The next 'THEN' says to move 2 spaces farther from the target, so the Animate moves 2 spaces from Rook to space 1. Normally, moving out of a space adjacent to an opponent would provoke a Break Attack, but the AI Step instructions specifically state that this movement does not provoke Break Attacks.
This concludes the Animate's turn, if there was another Animate on the board it would now take its turn.

verbatim_text:
Other Important Rules

SKILL CHECKS
Special Encounter Rules and Adventure Mechanics will sometimes require Adventurers or Combatants to make Skill Checks. These Skill Checks represent various non-combat challenges the players may be faced with. Depending on whether the figure is an Adventurer or an INTELLIGENT Combatant, the rules for making a Skill Check are different. Skill Checks might require a specific figure, multiple figures, or a random figure to pass them. Whether a Skill Check passes or fails, the instructions will tell the players how to proceed.

ADVENTURER SKILL CHECKS
To make a Skill Check, the Adventurer rolls 2 PURPLE and adds the appropriate Skill Value (Example: Perception, Strength, Lore, etc.) from their Adventurer Card. If the total is equal to or greater than the listed Skill Check, they pass. Some Abilities will modify Skill Checks or Skill Values. Only Abilities with a Passive Condition Tag may modify Skill Checks that occur outside of Encounters. In these cases, the Ability must also be used by an Adventurer currently in the Active Party. Sometimes an Adventure Mechanic might call for a Combined Skill Check. In these cases, all figures specified to make the Check roll separate Skill Check and add their totals to determine if they all passed or all failed.

COMBATANT SKILL CHECKS
Combatants may have to make Skill Checks. COMMAND Combatants, Loyal Esper, and Conduits can all make Skill Checks the same as Adventurers. However, since INTELLIGENT Combatants do not have printed Skill Values like all the other cards, anytime an INTELLIGENT Combatant is required to make a Skill Check they will roll the BLACK. Any roll other than the SKULL is considered to pass the Check.

IMPORTANT: An INTELLIGENT Combatant will never jump more than 2 spaces in a single Jump Check. If the condition of an Intelligent Combatant's Step would require a Jump of more than 2 spaces, then the condition is considered false.

JUMPING
During an Adventurer's movement, they may choose to Jump over spaces which they would otherwise prefer to not move through.
Jumping is defined as moving over 1 or more spaces without being affected by the Terrain's effects (Reduced Movement, being Defeated, etc).
Jumping may only be done during a Move Action or Free Movement and Jumping over spaces expends Movement Points in the same way Movement does.
During Movement, an Adventurer declares that they are Jumping. Designate a space for the Adventurer to end their Jump on. Each space Jumped over requires a Movement Point, just like normal movement.
The space being Jumped out of must be an unoccupied Normal Terrain space.
The space(s) being Jumped over cannot be occupied by another figure.
The space being Jumped into may be any type of Terrain (other than Obstructing), but cannot be occupied by another figure.
To check if the Jump was successful, make an Agility 10 Skill Check. For each additional space Jumped over after the first, add +2 to the difficulty of the Skill Check.
If 1 or more allies are adjacent to the space the Adventurer is Jumping out of, they may add a single ally's Strength to their roll when making the Skill Check, as the ally gives them a boost.
If an Adventurer fails the Skill Check and an ally is adjacent to the space they are Jumping into, the ally may attempt to catch them by making a Perception Skill Check with a difficulty equal to the difficulty of the Agility Check that was failed.
If an Adventurer fails the Skill Check and an ally does not pass a Perception Check to catch the Adventurer, or if there isn't an Adventurer to try and catch them, the Adventurer lands on the first space they attempted to Jump over and the Ability or Action that granted the Movement ends. Both Move Actions and Free Movement can no longer be made by the Adventurer during the remainder of their turn.
If the Adventurer passes the Skill Check, place the Adventurer's figure on the space they chose when starting their Jump. The Adventurer then continues their Movement.

IMPORTANT: If a figure fails a Jump Check that includes any Terrain that would otherwise Defeat them, and they are not caught by an ally, that figure is Defeated regardless of what space they started the Jump Check from.

Example: If Zeke Jumps over A and then continues to Jump over B, he would make two Agility 10 checks. If he failed either of these Skill Checks, he would immediately end his Move Action in the first space he failed to Jump over.

OTHER IMPORTANT RULES contmued oy,

LARGE BASE FIGURES

Some figures occupy more than 1 space. These figures are called Large

Based Figures and have special rules associated with their large size.

¢ When drawing Line of Sight, Range, or SOI to or from a Large Based
Figure, you must use a single space their figure occupies. The figure
making the Action or using the Ability may choose which space to
use. Intelligent Combatants will always use the most beneficial space.

* Large Based Figures are only affected by Terrain (except Obstructing
Terrain), when each space their base occupies is inside of the same
type of Terrain. Exceptions are listed on the Terrain in question. See
Table 7: Terrain Types, Pg. 96.

¢ When moving, count each space one at a time like normal. A Large
Based Figure may not move into any space unless every space its base
occupies could be placed following all the normal rules of movement.

* Large Based Figures can occupy different Elevations at once. When
moving, at least one space their base occupies must be considered and is
still subject to all the rules of moving up or down Elevation. An Elevation
change of 3 or more will only Defeat a Large Based Figure if no other
space it occupied made an Elevation change of less than 3.

* Large Based Figures spawned will DISPLACE other figures.

* Large Based Figures placed on the board via an Ability (e.g. WARP,
SUMMONING, CONDUITS) will DISPLACE other figures.

«Ifa Large Based Figure is too large to be Spawned or placed by an
Ability due to Obstructing Terrain, place them on the closest set of
spaces that would not result in their entire base occupying Dangerous
Terrain instead. Then, DISPLACE other figures.

* When instructed to Spawn a Large Based Figure on a space smaller
than its base size, place their figure so that its base occupies at least
one of the non-Dangerous space(s) depicted/instructed.

REDUCING NUMBERS

No Value can be reduced below 0. This includes Attack rolls, Damage,
Range, or any other number. If an Effect, Ability, or Action would reduce
a value below 9, that value is 0 instead.

ROUNDING NUMBERS

Anytime you must cut a number in half, you always round up to the
nearest whole number. This could be Damage, Gold, or any other number
in the game.

COMPANIONS

Companions represent characters in the story that help out the players in
the Adventure Mode. Typically, these will be found in the Hidden Card
deck. These cards do not count against an Adventurer's Item limits, but an
Adventurer is limited to having only 1 Companion equipped. Companions
can not be Stored in the Pack, but they may be Stored in the Party Stash,

RE-ROLLING DICE

When using an Ability that re-rolls a roll, or a specific die, you must use
this Ability during when the roll or die in question is rolled. You may not
wait until a later step of the occurring Action. Once this roll or die has
been chosen and re-rolled, the new value must be kept. Alternatively, if
you choose not to re-roll the roll or specific die, you may not choose to
do so after the step of the Action or effect of the roll has been resolved.
There is no limit to the amount of times a die or roll may be re-rolled.

FORCED MOVEMENT

Some Abilities may refer to "Forced Movement". Forced Movement is
defined as any Movement a Combatant makes that they had no choice

in making. This includes being moved via Push, Pull, Command, or via
Terrain Effects or Special Encounter Rules such as Currents. Additionally,
it's possible for a Combatant to use an Ability that moves them an amount
of spaces as part of the Ability text. If this Movement is not listed as
optional (i.e "you may") or as "up to" an amount of spaces, this is also
considered Forced Movement. Movement made via a Move Action

or Symbol Ability controlled gy the combatant is always considered
Voluntary.

Familiars are not affected by Disciplines or Effects that might prevent them from being used by their master.

The Felled Afterlife Discipline allows Adventurers to bring up to two Enslaved Spirits to the board under their control.
Enslaved Spirits are Command Cards that function like other Command Cards.
Adventurers can only have one Command Combatant on the board at a time.

core_rules.mechanic_description: An Adventurer earns a CONDUIT Command Card when they are within SOL of an opponent who is Defeated and has a corresponding CONDUIT Command Card.
An Adventurer can use a CONDUIT Command Card when they are within SOL of a Defeated opponent who has a corresponding CONDUIT Command Card.
An Adventurer replaces their Adventurer Card with a CONDUIT Command Combatant Card of their choosing when using Conduit Summoning.
An Adventurer cannot use or gain the benefit of Disciplines, Items, or Abilities other than Conduit Summoning while in Conduit Form.
An Adventurer must use the new Conduit's listed Skills when making Skill Checks while in Conduit Form.
An Adventurer cannot use Abilities, Skills, or Stamina Point Recovery until they return to their original Form.
Any Effect, Ability, or Damage tokens on the Adventurer carry over to their new CONDUIT Command Card.
An Adventurer can use Standard Actions and Abilities while in Conduit Form.
An Adventurer can swap their CONDUIT Command Card back to their Adventurer Card at any time.
An Adventurer can stay in their chosen CONDUIT Form until they use the Discipline to swap their cards back, are instructed to Restore, or are Defeated.
An Adventurer can swap from one CONDUIT Form into another CONDUIT Form.
Any Effect, Ability, or Damage tokens that were on the Adventurer carry over back to their Adventurer Form when swapping back to their Adventurer Card.
Command Combatant Cards with the CONDUIT Tag follow all the normal rules of a Command Combatant.

The Conduit Summoning Discipline allows an Adventurer to physically
take on the aspects of another creature by melding their souls for a brief
moment. This grants the Adventurer access to many new and varied
Abilities at the detriment of losing their own.

Middara contains Command Combatant Cards with the CONDUIT Tag.

THE BASICS

As players progress through Middara, some Combatants might get
stronger, randomly switch up their Al, or even be replaced by entirely
different types of Combatants. The following section details the special
rules to denote this Spawning behavior.

These rules replace the Alternate Tag rules from our previous versions

of Middara. If you're using a previous version of Middara, or other
promotional material, all Alternate Tag Combatants now Spawn according
to the rules below. However, mechanically, they still function as described

All Combatants now have a Loot Level printed on the front and back

core_rules.mechanic_description: Combatant Cards with the Alternate Tag will always specify a Base Combatant they might replace. These Combatant Cards are considered Alternate Combatants.

Alternate Combatants are mechanically and thematically different creatures in Middara that can be used as random substitutes for Base Combatants. These substitutes add variety to your game and shake up existing content in exciting and unpredictable ways.

core_rules.mechanic_description: On the back of Combatants with the Alternate Tag, there is the name of the Base Combatant Cards they are considered Possible Spawns for.
Combatants with the Alternate Tag have special Spawn rules associated with them. See Possible Spawns, Pg. 80.
Combatant Cards rely on having their prerequisites met before they can be Spawned. The common Prerequisites found across all Combatant Cards are as follows:
Additional Prerequisites - This represents additional unique Prerequisites that must be met before this card might be used under specified circumstances.
Variation: Cave Sickle (Group 1-3) | Loot LVL: Mundane. Additional Prerequisites: This card is only ever used as a Variation after you've attempted the Bounty, The Cave Sickle Queen.
Combatant Cards are considered Possible Spawns if they have been revealed, meet all their listed prerequisites, and they are not currently being used.

When Setting Up an Encounter during the Placement Phase, don't check for Possible Spawns. Meaning, you must place the figures as listed in the Setup Diagram. Or if a Combatant Card Spawns a named Combatant Card.
However, in all other cases, when a figure requires a new Combatant Card to Spawn, a Possible Spawn must be considered and might Spawn instead.

This includes Diagrams, Totems, or even when a Summoner summons an Opposing Esper. To determine what Spawns, you'll shuffle all the Possible Spawns together and draw one randomly. If there are more Spawns required to finish placing the required amount of figures, repeat this process until the amount of figures called for are Spawned. See Important Possible Spawn Rules, Pg. 82.

THE ALTERNATE TAG

Combatant Cards with the Alternate Tag will always specify a Base
Combatant they might replace. These Combatant Cards are considered
Alternate Combatants.

Alternate Combatants are mechanically and thematically different
creatures in Middara that can be used as random substitutes for Base
Combatants. These substitutes add variety to your game and shake up
existing content in exciting and unpredictable ways.

On the back of Combatants with the Alternate Tag, there is the name
of the Base Combatant Cards) they are considered Possible Spawns for
listed as ALTERNATE: X. (e.g. Cave Sickle.)

An Alternate Combatant will only ever list Base Combatants as a possible
Combatant they might replace. Meaning, there is no situation in which an
Alternate Combatant can replace another Alternate Combatant.

Since Alternate Combatant Cards are thematically considered their
own creature, they will never share Groups with Base Combatant
Cards. Meaning, you will never consider Groups as a prerequisite when
determining if an Alternate Combatant is a Possible Spawn.

Combatants with the Alternate Tag have special Spawn rules associated
with them. See Possible Spawns, Pg. 80.

be Spawned. The common Prerequisites found across all Combatant

POSSIBLE SPAWNS

Combatant Cards are considered Possible Spawns if they have been

When Setting Up an Encounter during the Placement Phase, don't check

instead.

This includes Diagrams, Totems ,or even when a Summoner summons an
Opposing Esper.

To determine what Spawns, you'll shuffle all the Possible Spawns together
and draw one randomly. If there are more Spawns required to finish
placing the required amount of figures, repeat this process until the
amount of figures called for are Spawned. See Important Possible Spawn
Rules, Pg. 82.

Abraxis Battle Dice is a mini-game that players can take part in during the
Adventure Mode. It uses Abraxis cards, the custom dice, Damage tokens,
and $P tokens.

Each Adventurer gets 4 dice: Give one Adventurer 2 WHITE @ and

2 PURPLE &% dice. Another gets 2 TEAL @ and 2 ORANGE & dice.
Another gets 2 GREEN @ and 2 RED & dice. And the last gets 2 BLUE
@ and 2 GREY & dice. Each player also starts with 10 Abraxis Points and
5 Fate tokens. These may be tracked with Damage tokens and $P tokens
respectively.

The game takes place through a series of 5 Rounds. The goal of each
Round is for Adventurers to roll their dice and have the Symbols on all 4
of their dice match the Symbols printed on the bottom of the Abraxis card
they are facing as closely as possible.

At the end of each Round, if an Adventurer fails to match the Symbols on
the Abraxis card, they lose Abraxis Points. When an Adventurer loses all
their Abraxis Points, they are out of the game.

If Adventurers can match their Symbols well enough to survive these 5
Rounds, they'll be rewarded. Rewards earned via Abraxis Battle Dice are
cumulative. Meaning, that if all 4 Adventurers survive, they would gain
the rewards listed for all four tiers. (1 Adventurer, 2 Adventurer, etc.)

1. ROLL FOR SYMBOLS:

Each Round, Adventurers will simultaneously roll all 4 of their dice and
must Lock In the result of 1 die.

When dice are Locked In, this means that the Adventurer is satisfied with
the result of that die and has set it aside to be tallied against the Abraxis
card's Symbols at the end of the Round. All dice that are Locked In will
not be rolled again.

If an Adventurer would like to Lock In the result of more than 1 die, they
may spend 1 of their 5 Fate tokens. For each Fate token they spend, they
may Lock In an extra die.

If an Adventurer does not want to Lock In any of the dice they rolled, they
may spend 1 Fate token to skip Locking In any of their dice.

Once all Adventurers have decided which dice to Lock In, or after they've
decided to not Lock In any by spending 1 of their 5 Fate tokens, they will
then simultaneously roll all of their remaining (non-Locked fn) dice.

After rolling a second time, Adventurers will again decide which single
die they would like to Leck In, Fate tokens may be spent the same way as

‘VARIANTS AND THEIR PURPOSE

Middara is a huge game and there are tons of ways we've playtested
it over the years. There are many ways to handle common mechanical
issues. Some of these options we considered might have worked well
despite us deciding to not use them in the Rulebook.

For those looking to tune their Middara experience we've provided some
of these options. All of which we've playtested enough to give some of
our own feedback and experiences.

Any of the following rules can be taken a la carte to modify Middara to
turn it into the game best suited for your gaming group.

NO PLAYER ELIMINATION

Middara was designed in such a way that player elimination is an
essential part of the game balance. For those who would prefer to remove
it, we've provided a way to do so while still providing an experience
close to the one we intended.

Normally, the only ways players can Lose Encounters in Middara are A:
All Adventurers in the Encounter are Defeated, B: Via a Special Encounter
Rule, or C: Players add a 4th Urgency token to the back of the Initiative
Track.

To remove player elimination, use the following rules:
Anytime an Adventurer is Defeated, do the following:

* Remove their figure from the game board and place it on their
Initiative Card.

¢ Remove all Ability and Effect tokens from their card.

* Add an Urgency token to the back of the Initiative Track.

On the Defeated Adventurer's next turn, do the following:

e Place the Adventurer on an unoccupied space within an ally's SOL

* Remove Damage tokens until they have Damage tokens equal to half
of their max HP.

* The returned Adventurer takes their turn as normal, Gaining Stamina
Points (SP) and following all other steps as if they had not been
Defeated.

This Variant could make the game harder, depending on your group's
playstyle and how prone they are to getting Urgency tokens already.

To tweak this difficulty, change the amount of Urgency Tokens required to

lose an Encounter.
© 5 Urgency Tokens: Easy
Ae 4 Urgency Tokens: Normal

the 2 and 3 player variants of
iddara.com. The rules and thei

5TH PLAYER

Group size may vary between players and while Middara does not
natively support 5 players, players may choose to play with 5 people
anyway.
The main reason Middara does not natively support 5 players is because
at the beginning of the Adventure, there are only 4 characters available to
play. A 5th player, therefore, would have to wait until another Adventurer
joins the Party. That would create too much downtime for one of the
players.
However, if you happen to have access to another Adventurer from
another Middara product and are okay with the narrative dissonance of
a never-mentioned party member, you may play the game with 5 players
using the following rules:
¢ The 5th Adventurer starts each Encounter adjacent to the Starting
Zone listed in the Encounter Setup.
¢ = The maximum HP for all non-BOSS opponents is increased by 50%.
The maximum HP for all BOSS opponents is increased by 25%.
For Example, a Cave Sickle would have 9 maximum HP and
an Earth Loa would have 30 maximum HP.
This is not the recommended way to play Middara as it will likely make
for a much easier experience and increase down time.

FORGIVING DANGEROUS TERRAIN

Any time an Adventurer would be Pushed, Pulled, or Commanded onto
or through Dangerous Terrain, instead of being immediately Defeated,
they may make an Agility Check to Jump to a space they have not moved
into this turn. If they succeed this check, they may place their figure on
the chosen space. If they fail this check, or there is no space available to
Jump too, they are Defeated like normal.

Intelligent Combatants follow this same rule. However, when rolling, they
succeed on any symbol but the SKULL.

RE-SPECING AN ADVENTURER

Occasionally, players will realize that a different Discipline will work
better for their Adventurer or they may simply want to try going a different
direction with how an Adventurer functions.

Ifa player would like to change the Disciplines their Adventurer has
learned, they may do so any time they Shop and Train by spending 25
Gold, plus another 25 gold for every Loot Level beyond Mundane the

Middara was designed to provide a challenging experience for all types of
players. However, some people may find the game too hard or too easy.
The following rules are ways to modify the difficulty of the game.

Use any or all of these rules for an easier or harder experience. These

are listed in the overall potency of the rule with the top rule making the
biggest difference to difficulty.

health may remove a total of 12 damage tokens split between
the Adventurers in the Active Group, An Adventure can only

For An Easier Experience

* No Scaling: Do not use Combatants of the higher Loot LVL. Instead,

Combatant they are thematically tied to takes the same amount of

ALTERNATE, VARIATION, LOOT LEVEL (LVL):
Combatants with this Tag have special rules on how and when they Spawn.
See Alternate, Variations, and Loot LVL Pg. 79.

AVARICE (X):

These Combatants carry more wealth than your average Combatant. When
an Adventurer Defeats a Combatant with the AVARICE Tag, they draw extra
Combatant Loot Cards. The X represents the amount of extra cards drawn.
For example, an AVARICE 1 Combatant would give 2 Combatant Loot Cards
instead of the normal 1.

BOSS:

Combatants with this tag represent particularly strong opponents, players
will fight these Combatants during special Encounters throughout both the
Adventure Mode and Crawl Mode. BOSS Combatant Cards are located in
Hidden Card decks and will be revealed whenever a Special Encounter Rule
instructs players to reveal and use it. Some BOSS Combatants have special
Monster Loot that players will Gain when the BOSS is Defeated. If this does
occur, a Special Encounter Rule will instruct players on how to Gain this
Monster Loot. Unless otherwise stated, Bosses drop Combatant Loot as
normal. If you draw the Monster Loot Card, you must redraw.

CONDUIT:

Combatant Cards with this Tag are used by Adventurers using the Conduit
Summoning Discipline. The Adventurer that used Conduit Summoning
controls the Combatant Card with this Tag.

FRAGILE:

When calculating the total 3 HP of a LOYAL ESPER with this Tag, half the total
HP calculated.

GILDED:
These Combatants always give their Monster Loot instead of a Combatant
Loot Card.

LOYAL ESPER:

Combatants with this Tag can be Spawned by Adventurers through the use of
the Summoning Discipline. The Adventurer that Spawned a Combatant with
this Tag controls the Combatant they Spawned. These cards use special rules,
see Summoning Pg. 75.

OPPOSING ESPER:

Intelligent Combatants with this Tag can be Spawned by enemy summoners
or might start on the board during setup. These cards use special rules. See
Opposing Espers Pg. 76.

SWARM:

When a SWARM Combatant is Defeated, no Combatant Loot is drawn
unless it was the last Combatant of its kind in a Group and its Initiative
Card is removed. For example, if there is only 1 Cave Sickle left in a Group,
and that Cave Sickle is Defeated, the corresponding Cave Sickle Group's
Initiative Card is removed, and the Adventurers Gain a Combatant Loot
Card.

TRIVIAL:
When a TRIVIAL Combatant is Defeated, no Combatant Loot is drawn.

TYPE (X):
A Combatant thematic designation. See Type Tag Pg. 82.

VARIATION (X):
A Combatant thematic designation. See Type Tag Pg. 82.

SQUEEZE:

Figures with SQUEEZE represent figures that are very large but who are
also intelligent enough to avoid obstacles with effort and cunning.

A figure with SQUEEZE may attempt to move into 1x1 spaces if
Obstructing Terrain would otherwise prevent them from fitting. To do so,
during a Move Action, a figure with SQUEEZE may spend 1 additional SP
to count all movement granted by that Move Action as though their figure
only occupied a single space. A figure may only squeeze through spaces

in this way if each space counted would prevent them from fitting due to
Obstructing Terrain only.

A figure with SQUEEZE may not willingly end their Move Action in a
space that they cannot fit in. If something would cause them to end their
turn in a space they can not fit in, end the current Action and all Abilities.
Then, the figure with SQUEEZE is placed on the closest legal space they've
moved into this Move Action/Ability and Dealt 6 IRREDUCIBLE DMG. If
required, this could move them into the spaces they started this movement.

SUBTERFUGE:
A Discipline Tree. See Discipline Trees Pg. 32.

SUMMONER x:
A Tag referenced by Opposing Espers to determine their Force Values. See
Opposing Espers Pg. 76.

SWAP:

The figure using this Ability is removed from the board and the target of
this Ability is removed from the board. They are then placed in the space
the other occupied. This does not provoke Break Attacks.

SYMBIOTIC:

A figure with the Symbiotic Tag represents a single figure that uses 2 or
more Combatant Cards. These Combatants can be in 1 or more groups on
1 of more unique Combatant Cards.

When taking turns, Symbiotic Combatants will use the same figure on the
board. Meaning, they draw Line of Sight, target others, and follow all the
same rules as if they were considered a single figure. When provoking
Break Attacks, all Symbiotic Combatants may make Break Attacks. When
making Skill Checks that would affect more than one Symbiotic Combatant
(e.g. Jumping), all Symbiotic Combatants must make the Check. When
choosing a Symbiotic figure as a target, you must choose 1 of the
Symbiotic Combatants that share that figure as the target.

If an Action or Ability would target 1 or more adjacent spaces that

still contain the Symbiotic figure, they may target another Symbiotic
Combatant for each additional space that would affect the Symbiotic
figure. If an Ability would target all figures within SOI or Range, then all
Symbiotic Combatants would be affected. A Symbiotic Combatant's figure
is removed from the Encounter via Defeat only if all associated Symbiotic
Combatants that share the figure are also Defeated.

THROW : (DIE):

The Throw Ability allows an Adventurer to deal PHYSICAL DMG to an
opponent equal to the listed die within Range 4 and Line of Sight. This is
NOT an Attack and no Attack roll is made. You simply roll the die and deal
the Damage. As such, this Damage cannot be Dodged. Lastly, Armor still
reduces Damage dealt this way.

UNSTOPPABLE:

While moving, this figure treats Obstructing Terrain as normal spaces.
Replace any Obstructing Terrain this figure moves into with Hindering
Terrain.

VARIATION:

See Alternate, Variations, and Loot LVL PG. 79.

WARP:

The targets) affected by this Ability are removed from their current
location and then placed in a new location as designated by the Ability
text. Locations can be a space on the board or any component outside of
the board (e.g. Combatant cards, Initiative cards, etc.). WARP does not
provoke Break Attacks.

WANDERING:

Items with this Tag and Tier cannot be purchased. Instead, they can only
be found. When you are drawing Combatant Loot and Pull the Unique
Loot card, shuffle this card into the Unique Loot deck as one of the options
regardless of the current Loot Level. This Item can be sold as though it
were an Item of your current Loot LVL. However, Wandering Items are
intended to be limited by the number of copies included in the game as
they're thematically Unique.

Note: There are no Wandering Items included in this Base Game
(Unintentional Malum).

Weapons have Tags that thematically categorize them. Example: SWORD,
WARHAMMER, TOME, etc. Mechanically, these are referenced by other tags
such as COMBO or when calculating a RESISTANCE.

Some figures may Burrow, or become Burrowed. When a figure Burrows, replace the figure with the corresponding sized Burrow token.
When a figure is instructed to Un-Burrow, replace the Burrow token with its corresponding figure and DISPLACE any figures that would be
occupying its space. See the DISPLACE Tag Pg. 92.
A Burrowed figure:
Has RESISTANCE : PHYSICAL DMG and MAGICAL DAMAGE and cannot Flank or be Flanked.
Does not provoke Break Attacks and may not make Break Attacks. Un-burrowing or Burrowing does not provoke Break Attacks.
Moved by an Ability (e.g. Push) must Un-Burrow instead. All subsequent movement caused by this Ability is resolved like normal.
Meaning, a Burrowed figure who is Pushed 2 spaces would Un-Burrow, then be Pushed 1 space like normal.
Given the option to Jump to prevent themselves from being Defeated will immediately Un-Burrow to take advantage of this.
May not enter Water, Obstructing, or Dangerous Terrain. If an Ability would force them into Water, Obstructing, or Dangerous Terrain,
they must Un-Burrow. They would also be subject to that Terrain's rules associated with being moved into it. (e.g. Damage if it's
Obstructing Terrain or being Defeated if it was Dangerous Terrain.)
Ignores Elevation and all other types of Non-Dangerous Terrain.
Ignores all other Un-Burrowed figures and may end their turn on spaces containing other Un-Burrowed figures.
Does not block Line of Sight or movement of Un-Burrowed figures. Meaning, an Un-Burrowed figure may end their movement on a
Burrowed figure.

adjacent to the Bulb,
Bulb tokens that are moved at the same time as another figure or cause a situation where a Break Attacks timing is ambiguous will not flip.
Both Adventurers and Combatants might use Abilities that place Dynamite tokens on the board.
Dynamite tokens are tokens that will explode and deal Damage to all those near them. Dynamite tokens exist in one of two states, Lit and
Unlit. Anytime a Dynamite token is placed on the board for any reason it becomes Lit. Dynamite tokens that start on the board are already
Lit.
At the end of the next round after a Dynamite token becomes Lit it will explode. When a Dynamite token explodes, discard this token.
Then, all figures on or adjacent to the token are dealt 3 PURPLE (% of IRREDUCIBLE DMG and any Loot tokens on or adjacent to the
token are discarded. An Adventurer adjacent to a Lit Dynamite token may spend 1 SP to make a Presence 10 Check. If they pass, they
bravely pick up the Dynamite, which stays Lit.
An Adventurer with a Lit or Unlit Dynamite token may spend 1 SP to place a Dynamite token on any space within Range 4 and Line of
Sight. Opponents block this Line of Sight, but allied figures do not.
Dynamite tokens that a figure has are considered to be occupying the same space as that figure. Any Dynamite token caught in the
explosion of another Dynamite token also explodes. (Including any unlit Dynamite equipped or in your Pack.)

Table 11: STEPS FOR MAKING AN ATTACK
STEPS FOR MAKING AN ATTACK

1, CHOOSE THE TARGET
Select a single figure within Line of Sight and Range as the target.

2. BUILD THE COMBAT DICE POOL
Attacker uses dice printed on their equipped Weapons. 1-Handed Weapons have a
single dice. 2-Handed Weapons have two dice.

3. EMPOWER
Adventurer or a Command Combatant may spend 1 SP to EMPOWER the Attack. If
they do, add BLACK % to the Combat Dice Poo!

4, DODGE

a. Check if the target Dodges. {If the target is an Adventurer or Command
Combatant they may spend 1 SP to Dodge. If the target is an Intelligent
Combatants they only Dodge when instructed to do so.)

b. Make a Dodge Roll by rolling BLACK % and adding 1 Defense for each B
rolled.

ROLL TO HIT

a, Make an Attack Roll

b. Spend Symbols & use Abilities to add to the Attack roll.

c. Determine if you Hit. (Rolled equal to or greater than the targets Defense.) If
you did, continue to Step 6a. Determine Damage. If you missed, continue to Step
6e. Check if the Target Counters.

. DETERMINE DAMAGE
a. Calculate the difference by which your Attack Hit and add it as Damage.
b. Spend Symbols & use Abilities that add to the Damage of an Attack.
cc. Subtract the target's Armor.
d. Calculate & Deal Final Damage.
e. If the Attack misses or deals no Final Damage check if the Target Counters. If
they do, the Attack immediately ends. If the Attack missed and the target did not
Counter, the Attacker skips step 7. Use Follow Up Abilities and continues to step
8. Resolve the Attack.

7. Use Follow Up Abilities
Using a FU Ability that starts a new Action ends the Attack.

8. Resolve the Attack
The current Attack ends.

NOTE: For complete rules and details See The Attack Action Pg. 41.

Table 12: PHASES OF AN ADVENTURER’S TURN
PHASES OF AN ADVENTURER'S TURN

1. START OF TURN PHASE:
Resolve Abilities and Effects that occur at the start of a turn.

2. STATUS PHASE:
Any Effects and Abilities that have the 323059 Tag occur during this Phase. See
Pg. 95 for a list of Effects.

3. REFRESH PHASE:
During the Refresh Phase, the Adventurer goes through the following steps:
A. Recover Stamina Points (SP):
Each Adventurer’s Stamina Recovery Bar determines how many $P they receive
during this step, as well as how many SP they may have at any given time. See A:
Stamina Recovery Bar on Pg. 25.
|IMPORTANT: Adventurers do not Gain SP during the Refresh
Phase of their Ist tum of an Encounter. See Prepare Phase Pg. 14.
B. Un-Exhaust Cards:
Some Abilities require the Adventurer to B EXHAUST them to be used. During the
Refresh Phase, any Exhausted cards are Un-Exhausted.

4, ACTION PHASE:

During the Action Phase, an Adventurer may spend SP to take Actions and/or use
Abilities. When they decide they no longer want to spend SP or take Actions and/or
use Abilities, the Adventure continues to the End of Turn Phase.

5. END OF TURN PHASE:
Resolve Abilities and Effects that occur at the End of a Turn.

Table 13: STEPS FOR CASTING A SPELL
STEPS FOR CASTING A SPELL

1, CHOOSE THE TARGET(S)
Select a single figure within SOI as the target. Some Abilities have specific targeting
parameters that may override this or allow you to target more than 1 figure.

2. DETERMINE THE FORCE
The Force of a SPELL determines how difficult the Spell’s effects are to resist.

A. BUILD FORCE POOL: A Force Pool consists of a figure's printed Casting Die
or Upgrade,

B. EMPOWER: When casting a SPELL, an Adventurer or Command Combatant
may choose to spend 1 SP to EMPOWER the Spell. When Empowering a Spell,
add the BLACK ¥% to the Force Pool. When rolling to determine your Force, for
each [rolled on the BLACK @, add +1 to the Force of the Spell. Intelligent
Combatants will only EMPOWER a Spell if instructed to do so.

C. ROLLTO DETERMINE YOUR FORCE: Finally, the figure Casting the SPELL
rolls their Casting die and Empower Die if applicable, and adds the printed X
value on the Spell to the result. (Usually 6)

3. EACH TARGET MAKES A CONVICTION CHECK

Each Adventurer and Combatant Card has Conviction Dice printed on it. These

2 dice determine how resistant a figure is to Spells. During this step, each target
makes a separate Conviction Check to resist the Spell’s effects.

To make a Conviction Check, each figure targeted by the Spell rolls the Conviction
dice printed on their card. If the total number rolled is equal to or greater than the
Spell's Force Value, the Spell is resisted by that figure. However, if the roll is less
than the Force Value of the Spell, the Spells printed effects occur. Once every target
has rolled a Conviction Check, the Spell Action ends.

4, RESOLVE THE SPELL’S EFFECT

Each target that failed their Conviction Check resolves the spell's effects separately
and in the order they made the Conviction Check. This could be Magic Damage
determined by a roll, Negative Effects such as Poison, or manipulating their position
ona ile. A Spell's effects are described on the Ability that started the Spell Action
after, "Cast a SPELL (X)".

NOTE: For complete rules and details See The Spell Action Pg. 53.
